question: One of the processes from the ready state will be chosen by the OS depending upon the scheduling algorithm and placed in _______ state for execution.
solution:
The correct answer is __**running**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Ready state:** In this state, processes are waiting for CPU allocation to execute their instructions.
 
• The operating system uses scheduling algorithms to choose a process from the ready state.
 
• **Running state:** The chosen process moves to the running state, where it gets executed.
 
• Processes transition between states (ready, running, wait, etc.) based on the OS's control and resource availability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Scheduling algorithms:** These include FCFS (First-Come-First-Serve), SJF (Shortest Job First), Round Robin, and Priority Scheduling.
 
• **Wait state:** A process moves to this state if it is waiting for I/O or other resources to become available.
 
• **New state:** This is the state where a process has been created but is not yet ready for execution.
 
• **Suspend state:** A process may be moved to this state if it needs to be temporarily halted.
